---
title: "Definition-style theorems have an upright body in the simple appearance"
format: typst
keep-typ: true
_quarto:
  tests:
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        -
          # plain style: bold header, italic body
          - '#let simple-theorem-render\(prefix: none, title: "", full-title: auto, body\) = \{(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){4}\s*emph\(body\)'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"theorem",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-theorem-render,'
          # definition style: bold header, upright body
          - '#let simple-definition-render\(prefix: none, title: "", full-title: auto, body\) = \{(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){4}\s*body(\r\n?|\n)'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"definition",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-definition-render,'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"exercise",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-definition-render,'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"example",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-definition-render,'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"algorithm",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-definition-render,'
        -
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"theorem",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-definition-render,'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"definition",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-theorem-render,'
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"algorithm",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){3}\s*render: simple-theorem-render,'
      ensurePdfRegexMatches:
        -
          - 'Exercise 1 \(Mean\)\.'
          - 'Definition 1\.'
          - 'Theorem 1\.'
        - []
---

In the `simple` appearance, which the documentation describes as classic
LaTeX style, theorems in the amsthm `plain` style have an italic body, and
theorems in the `definition` style (definitions, examples, exercises and
algorithms) have an upright body.

::: {#exr-a}
## Mean

Compute the mean of the following data.

| x | y |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
:::

::: {#def-b}
A definition.
:::

::: {#exm-c}
An example.
:::

::: {#thm-d}
A theorem.
:::

::: {#alg-e}
An algorithm.
:::
